title: Rav Huna bar Manoach
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He was Rava’s student and afterward came before Rav Papa, as in Taanit 9a: Rav Huna bar Manoach, Rav Shmuel bar Idi and Rav Chiyya of Vastanya used to be before Rava. When Rava died, they came before Rav Papa. Whenever he told them a teaching that did not seem reasonable to them, they would signal to one another. Rav Papa was distressed, and in his dream he was made to read: “And I cut off the three shepherds.” The next day, when they took leave of him, he said to them: “Let the Rabbis go in peace” (so it is in Ein Yaakov).

Likewise he spoke in the name of Rav Acha son of Rav Ika, as in Megillah 25b, Gittin 24a and 64b, Bava Kamma 58a, Bava Metzia 71b, Sanhedrin 42a and Bekhorot 28b and 45b. In Yevamot 43a he spoke in the name of Rav Idi son of Rav Ika, and Hyman proposes Rav Acha; and in Bava Kamma 22a he spoke in Rav Ika’s name — Hyman proposes reading in the name of Rav Acha son of Rav Ika, as in Dikdukei Soferim’s reading.

He is mentioned in Nazir 51a: “Rav Huna bar Manoach asked”; in Gittin 51a and Menachot 101a he raises objections; and in Bava Kamma 19b they said, “If he tied it — on what account is he liable? Rav Huna bar Manoach said: on account of his pit that rolls.”

notes.text: Rava is the deceased first teacher and Papa is the later teacher distressed by the pupils’ gestures. Hyman’s Ein Yaakov ending does not itself assert that the three died. Acha/Idi/Ika transmission corrections remain his proposals.

The inspected story runs from Taanit 9a into 9b: Rava dies, the three pupils come before Papa, Papa is distressed, and the dream and farewell follow. The consulted text has בשלמא, whereas Hyman explicitly reports Ein Yaakov לשלמא; that exact Ein Yaakov edition was not inspected. The narrative does not state that the three died. Acha/Idi/Ika chain corrections remain Hyman’s proposals.
